route.name: Baghdad Railway
route.notes: Istanbul Haydarpaşa–Konya is technically the Anatolian Railway; the Baghdad Railway proper began at Konya. Kept together here as the through Istanbul–Basra corridor.  [established] Construction began 1903. Adana–Aleppo section opened 27 April 1912; the line reached Nusaybin by 1918 (still ~480 km short of completion in 1915); through completion to Baghdad only in 1940.  [route] TWO items from the project list need care: (1) GAZIANTEP and KARKAMIŞ belong to the MODERN Turkish reroute (a later Gaziantep–Karkamış line that bypasses Aleppo), not the original Ottoman main line, which ran Adana–Fevzipaşa–İslahiye–Meydan Ekbez–Aleppo. (2) KIRKUK is on a separate branch, not the Mosul–Baghdad main line (which runs via Baiji and Samarra). Both are retained as annotated extra_stations (off the main polyline). The classic alignment is used for the route geometry.  [gauge_mm] Standard gauge 1,435 mm (Adana–Aleppo confirmed).
route.history: The Ottoman Baghdad Railway, financed and engineered by Germany (Deutsche Bank; Philipp Holzmann), extended the Anatolian Railway from Konya toward Baghdad and ultimately Basra. Construction began 1903; the Adana–Aleppo section opened 27 April 1912; it reached Nusaybin by 1918 and was completed through to Baghdad only in 1940. Its defining engineering works were the Taurus and Amanus (Nur) mountain crossings, including the Ayran tunnel (~4.9 km, completed 1917; some sources cite ~8 km for the Ayran–Fevzipaşa crossing).
